# Multi-page floating-table native controls

Original manually authored controls, generated by `tools/multipage_floating_fixture.py`.
They reuse only the repository's original cell-end-context OPC skeleton. Native
PDFs were exported by the reference application with export-reference.ps1.
reference.json records native text positions and SHA-256 provenance.

The numeric-position controls now have passing native-coordinate comparisons in
`tests/browser/multipage-floating.spec.js`, including continuation-page editing,
export/reopen, package preservation and exact undo. Aligned multi-page positions,
multiple floating tables sharing one body flow, booklet pages and header/footer
anchors still retain the prior read-only fallback. Independent next-page section
flows are covered by `../section-floating-tables`; their tables no longer trigger
the shared-flow guard. The remaining combinations stay in scope.

Twelve controls vary page/margin/text vertical anchors, 24/96-point offsets and
omitted/default versus explicit compatibility mode 15. Each has a preceding body
paragraph, an 18-row table with 48-point minimum rows, and two following paragraphs.
Horizontal position is 72 points from the left margin, with a 216-point table.

Native observations: table fragments resume at the next page's text margin; the
body paragraph following the source table is on the final table page and wraps
beside it. The initial vertical offset, row cut and initial page depend on anchor
and compatibility mode. For example page-480 has two pages with default settings,
but page-480-15 has three: the table begins on page 2. These cases disprove simply
removing the single-page rejection while reusing a common origin on every page.

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.4.57 describes floating coordinates and the logical
anchor at the following regular paragraph. These controls investigate the native
pagination details not explicitly resolved by that positioning definition.
Broader collisions, alignment and section/story combinations remain required.

## Body-flow controls

`tools/multipage_floating_flow_fixture.py` derives six additional original controls
from the text/24-point controls, independently varying full text width, 60 short
following paragraphs, and absence of the preceding paragraph. Both compatibility
modes are retained. Their native PDFs and `flow-reference.json` record 14
pages, with text positions and source/PDF hashes. All six sources pass schema
validation; all native pages were visually inspected.

The full-width cases keep rows 00–11 on page 1 and rows 12–17 on page 2.
The following anchor starts below the final fragment, baseline 371.69 pt; it does
not move the first fragment down to that anchor's final position. In the narrow
long-following cases, following body text starts beside the final fragment on
page 2, then Body 52 starts page 3. None of those following paragraphs fills the
empty space beside the first table fragment. Removing the preceding paragraph
moves the first fragment up exactly 12 pt without changing the final-page anchor
or row cut. These observations hold in both tested compatibility modes.

Implementation implication: the pagination cursor at the table's source position
and the final position of its following paragraph must remain distinct. Appending
table pages after completing body pagination cannot reproduce these controls.
The engine now processes the table at its source position and resumes regular
paragraphs on the final fragment's page, then converges their side wrapping.

## Page starts, borders and row behavior

The start/border/rows generators and `record_multipage_floating.py` add fifteen
independent controls (32 native pages), for 33 controls and 71 native pages total.
All pages were visually inspected and all sources pass XML schemas. Native text
positions and hashes are recorded by group. The new controls establish:

- Modern page-relative tables above preceding body text move to the next page;
  the same table without preceding text starts on page 1. Above-margin placement
  does not increase the first fragment's row capacity.
- Page/margin placement clamps the first ordinary-sized fragment at the paper
  edge. Border width contributes to that limit. Text-relative offsets retain
  their distinct behavior.
- Legacy numeric horizontal positions identify the first cell's writing origin;
  modern positions identify the leading exterior border. Zero/one/three-point
  borders and explicit cell padding distinguish those origins. Continuation
  fragment bottom borders participate in wrap clearance.
- Header rows repeat on continuation pages; splittable long rows retain all
  paragraphs. A preceding keepNext paragraph must remain grouped with the next
  regular paragraph even when a single-page floating table sits between them.

Native comparisons use fixed 0.15-point horizontal and 0.2-point baseline
tolerances. They were not relaxed to accommodate implementation discrepancies.
